note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list. Guides, steps, kinds, missable flags and roadmap stages are written for this guide from those descriptions and the sources named beside each trophy.

trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it unlocks itself the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is no separate task to chase. Work through the roadmap in order — story first, then side missions, collectibles, activities and the combat and money trophies — and check the tracker as you go so nothing is left for a surprise second playthrough. Because every other trophy feeds this one, the fastest route is to follow the stage order and tick each trophy off as soon as it pops.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Earn all 54 other trophies in any order.
Follow the six roadmap stages so the grind trophies are spread across the playthrough.
Use the tracker's progress bar to confirm 54 of 54 before expecting the platinum.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this trophy comes from simply playing the start of the story and seeing that first job through to its end. Stay with the mission markers, follow the on-screen prompts, and do not worry about speed or style — finishing is all that counts. It is the first story trophy most players will earn and it cannot be missed, since the story cannot continue past it.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Start a new game and play through the opening until the Gone Fishing mission begins.
Follow the mission markers to each objective.
Finish the mission and the trophy pops at the debrief.

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is the first act of the story, and this trophy unlocks when its final mission is complete. Play the story missions in order — the game gates later chapters behind earlier ones, so there is no way to skip ahead and no way to miss this. If you are doing side content as it appears, keep an eye on the mission log so the chapter's closing mission is not left waiting while you wander Leonida.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Play every story mission in Chapter 1 in the order the game offers them.
Finish the chapter's final mission.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter closes.

trophies.guide: Chapter 2 continues the story after the first act, and this trophy is earned the same way as the last one: finish every story mission in the chapter until its closing mission is done. Nothing in the chapter needs a special approach — just keep following the story thread. Side activities unlock along the way, so this is a good chapter to start sampling them for the activity trophies later.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: Continue the story into Chapter 2.
Complete its missions in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission to unlock the trophy.

trophies.guide: By Chapter 3 the story moves into Vice City itself, and this trophy marks the end of that act. As with the earlier chapters, it is purely a matter of finishing the chapter's missions in order — the game will not let you reach Chapter 4 without it. Use this chapter to start banking progress on the longer grinds, like discovering vehicles and trying each activity type once, since Vice City puts most of them within easy reach.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Play through Chapter 3's story missions in order.
Try the new activities that open up in Vice City while you are there.
Complete the chapter's final mission.

trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale, and this trophy unlocks when its final mission is done. The missions here tend to be bigger set pieces, so keep a save from before each one if you want a clean retry, and stock up on armour and ammo between jobs. Once this pops, only the final mission stands between you and the gold story trophy.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Complete Chapter 4's missions in order.
Restock armour, ammo and snacks between the bigger set pieces.
Finish the chapter's closing mission.

trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the story's finish line: complete the final mission and it unlocks. Expect the finale to be the longest and hardest mission in the game, so go in prepared — full armour, a good weapon loadout, and a vehicle you trust for any driving section. There is no branching requirement here; finishing the mission once is enough, and if the ending offers a choice, the trophy is for completing the mission itself, not for picking a particular outcome.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
steps: Finish Chapters 1 to 4 to unlock the finale.
Prepare before starting: full armour, ammo and a reliable vehicle.
Complete the final mission to earn the gold trophy.

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and this trophy pops when you complete it. Like every story mission trophy, it cannot be missed: the mission appears in the story order and can be replayed from the mission menu if anything goes wrong on the first attempt. Follow the markers, do what the mission asks, and move on — the trophy is a checkpoint on the road through the story, not a side challenge.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Reach the Breakfast Run mission in the story order.
Complete all of its objectives.
The trophy unlocks at the mission's end.

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is one of the story's big heist missions, and completing it earns this trophy. Heists in this series usually have a setup phase followed by the job itself, so do the prep the game offers and take the approach that suits your loadout. The trophy is tied to finishing the mission, not to how cleanly you do it, so even a messy escape still counts as long as the mission completes.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Unlock The Cartel Heist by progressing the story.
Complete any setup the mission requires.
Finish the heist and escape to complete the mission.

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission, and finishing it unlocks this trophy. It sits in the story order, so you will reach it by playing through the chapters, and the mission replay menu covers you if the first attempt fails. Treat it like any other story mission: follow the objectives, and the trophy follows the completion screen.
trophies.name: Family Matters
steps: Reach the Child's Play mission in the story order.
Complete its objectives.
The trophy unlocks when the mission ends.

trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission, and this trophy is its completion reward. It arrives in the story order, so keep playing the main missions and it will come to you — there is no separate trigger to hunt down. If you fail partway through, the mission can be retried or replayed, so the trophy is safe as long as you finish the mission eventually.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
steps: Progress the story until the Headliners mission unlocks.
Complete the mission's objectives.
The trophy pops at the mission debrief.

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a named story mission set around the Vice City airport, and completing it earns this trophy. Airport missions tend to mix driving and shooting, so bring a fast vehicle and keep moving between cover. The trophy only cares that the mission is completed, so finish the takedown and the escape and it is yours.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
steps: Reach the VCIA Takedown mission in the story order.
Complete the takedown objectives at the airport.
Finish the mission and escape to unlock the trophy.

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a named story mission, and this trophy marks its completion. The name suggests a large-scale operation, so expect heavy opposition and plan for a longer fight: armour, a full weapon wheel, and patience between waves. As with the other story missions, finishing is what matters — complete it once and the trophy is locked in.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
steps: Unlock Operation Savage Glory through the story.
Stock up on armour and ammo before starting.
Complete the operation to earn the trophy.

trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the game's own 100% checklist, separate from the trophy list: it tracks story missions, side content, collectibles and activities, and it only hits 100% when every item on the in-game checklist is done. The surest path is to use the game's own completion stats screen as your master list and work through it category by category in the final cleanup stage, after the story is finished. Do not confuse it with the platinum — this one is about the game's internal completion percentage, and it is usually the last gold to pop before the platinum itself.
trophies.name: A Long Road
steps: Finish the story and all side mission strands first.
Open the in-game completion stats to see which categories are incomplete.
Clear each remaining category — collectibles, activities, stunts — until the stats read 100%.

trophies.guide: Stunts are the jumps, near-misses, airtime and other driving feats the game counts as you drive around Leonida, and this silver trophy needs 250 of them. The count builds up naturally across a full playthrough, but you can grind it deliberately: find a stretch of open road, chain jumps off ramps and near-misses in traffic, and repeat. A fast car and an open highway make the counter climb quickly, and the game shows your stunt total in the stats screen so you can track it.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
steps: Drive aggressively in open areas: jumps, airtime and near-misses all count.
Use a fast car on highways and ramps to chain stunts.
Check the stats screen for your stunt total and grind the remainder in one session.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Leonida offers a set of activity types — racing, fishing, arcade games, shooting ranges, drone races and more — and this trophy asks you to sample each type at least once. The practical approach is to open the map, visit one venue of each type, and complete a single round or attempt at each. You do not need to win or master any of them; one try each is enough, and the trophy pops as soon as the last type is sampled.
trophies.name: Master of None
steps: Open the map and note every activity type available.
Visit one venue of each type and complete a single attempt.
The trophy unlocks once every type has been tried.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shooting Range has 42 challenges, and this silver trophy requires a gold medal in every one of them. That means learning each challenge's scoring — accuracy and speed matter more than raw firepower — and replaying the ones you only bronze or silver until they are gold. Work through them range by range, use the weapon each challenge is built around, and take your time on the precision rounds rather than rushing the trigger.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Visit the Shooting Range and work through its 42 challenges.
Replay any challenge that is not yet gold, focusing on accuracy and speed.
Gold all 42 to unlock the silver trophy.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at a set of locations across Leonida, and this trophy needs a win at every one of them. Drone racing rewards smooth lines and clean cornering more than top speed, so learn each course's turns on a practice run before pushing for the win. The locations are spread across the map, so this pairs well with the exploration trophy — clear a location's race whenever you pass through.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Find the Top Fun drone race locations on the map.
Race each course, learning its turns before pushing for a win.
Win at every location to unlock the trophy.

trophies.guide: This trophy counts distinct races won, so winning the same race twenty times will not work — you need victories in 20 different events. Leonida's racing scene covers street races, off-road and more, and the wins can be spread across the whole playthrough. Pick the race types you are best at, upgrade a suitable vehicle for each, and keep a mental list of which events you have already won so you do not repeat one by mistake.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Enter races across the map in different event types.
Win each event once, tracking which ones are already done.
Reach 20 different race wins to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is a fishing rival, and this trophy comes from beating him in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are about timing and patience — watch the line, reel steadily, and do not let the fish snap it. Challenge Cal when you are comfortable with the fishing mechanics, ideally after a few practice catches, and the win counts as soon as the challenge ends in your favour.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
steps: Learn the fishing mechanics with a few casual catches first.
Find Cal and accept his fishing challenge.
Beat his catch to win the challenge and the trophy.

trophies.guide: Arcades around Leonida hold playable cabinet games, and this trophy needs you to finish just one of them. Pick the shortest or simplest cabinet you find — a quick arcade game is a low-effort trophy that fits neatly into an early exploration session. Walk up to a machine, play it through to its end, and the trophy pops when the game is complete.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade venue on the map.
Choose a cabinet game and play it through to completion.
The trophy unlocks when the game ends.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the side characters with a mission strand of his own, and this trophy unlocks when you finish the last mission in his chain. Side strands unlock as the story progresses, so keep checking the map for Andy's icon between story missions and work through his jobs in order. The final mission is the payoff — complete it and the strand closes with this trophy.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
steps: Unlock Andy's mission strand as the story progresses.
Complete his missions in order, watching the map for his icon.
Finish his final mission to earn the trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton has his own side mission strand, and this trophy is earned by completing its final mission. Like the other character strands, his jobs appear over the course of the story, so the trick is to keep returning to his marker whenever it shows on the map rather than leaving the whole strand for the end. Finish the chain's last job and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
steps: Find Kenton's strand on the map as it unlocks.
Work through his missions in order.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand is another side character chain, and this trophy unlocks at its final mission. His jobs tend to involve the open roads and rougher corners of Leonida, so bring a sturdy vehicle and expect chases. Play his missions in order as they appear, and the last one closes the strand with this trophy.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
steps: Unlock Billy's strand through story progress.
Complete his missions in order.
Finish his final mission to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers and Freaks missions are the odd jobs and encounters scattered across Leonida, each a short strand with its own characters. This silver trophy needs 8 complete strands, so it rewards exploring the map and stopping for every question-mark encounter you find. Some strands only appear after story progress or in specific areas, so sweep the map region by region and clear each stranger icon as you find it.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
steps: Explore the map and stop at every stranger encounter you find.
Complete each strand's missions in full — a half-finished strand does not count.
Finish 8 strands to earn the silver trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy is another side character with a mission chain, and this trophy comes from finishing its last mission. His strand unlocks during the story, so watch for his icon and clear his jobs as they appear rather than stockpiling them. The final mission closes his story and pops the trophy.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
steps: Unlock Randy's strand as the story progresses.
Complete his missions in order.
Finish his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's side strand ends with this trophy when you complete its final mission. His jobs appear on the map as the story advances, and each one leads into the next, so follow the chain through to its end. Clear his missions promptly when they show up and the finale will arrive in good time.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
steps: Find Tyrone's strand on the map as it unlocks.
Work through his missions in order.
Complete his final mission to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditation spots are quiet locations scattered across Leonida, and this trophy asks you to meditate at every one of them. They are a collectible in all but name: the work is finding them all, not the meditation itself, which is a short interaction at each spot. Use the map to sweep scenic overlooks, beaches and quiet corners, and meditate at each spot you find until the set is complete.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
steps: Look for meditation spots at scenic and quiet locations across the map.
Meditate at each spot you find.
Visit every spot to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret wants a unique animal hunted, and this trophy is earned by tracking that animal down and taking it. Hunting in this game means reading the terrain — look for tracks, listen for calls, and move quietly so the animal does not bolt before you are in range. Bring a scoped rifle, aim for a clean shot, and be patient: the unique animal is a single target, so a rushed approach that scares it off costs you the attempt.
trophies.name: Fair Game
steps: Find Bret and take the hunting job.
Track the unique animal using tracks and calls.
Take a clean shot to complete the hunt.

trophies.guide: Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida in sets, and this silver trophy needs 3 full sets completed. Cards hide in shops, interiors and out-of-the-way corners, so this is a sweep-the-map collectible best done with a checklist and a region-by-region pass. You do not need every card in the game — three complete sets is the bar — so focus on the sets whose cards you have already mostly found and finish those first.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Collect cards wherever you find them and note which sets they belong to.
Sweep regions one by one for the remaining cards of your nearest sets.
Complete 3 full sets to earn the silver trophy.

trophies.guide: WAiNK It is a location-based activity — find the spots, do the interaction, and move on — and this silver trophy needs 100 of them. The counter only climbs if you actually visit the locations, so fold this into your exploration: whenever the map shows a WAiNK spot nearby, stop and clear it. It pairs naturally with the explore-all-of-Leonida trophy, since both reward covering the whole map.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
steps: Find WAiNK It locations as you explore the map.
Use the interaction at each spot to count it.
Reach 100 locations to unlock the silver trophy.

trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's assorted side objectives — timed runs, stunt goals, combat trials and more — and this trophy needs 50 of them completed. The count is cumulative across every challenge type, so you do not need to master any one kind. Work through the challenge list in the menu, pick off the easiest ones first, and let the harder ones come naturally as you play; the total builds up fast once you start clearing them deliberately.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Open the challenge list and pick the easiest ones first.
Clear challenges across different types to build the count.
Complete 50 challenges to earn the trophy.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This trophy needs you and your partner to build up a 4-star wanted level together, then lose the police and escape. The risky part is the setup: you must reach 4 stars while your partner is with you, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. Use the countryside or the water to break pursuit, and avoid fighting back once you are trying to lose them — every new crime resets the escape timer.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner present and a 4-star wanted level in one run — a specific co-op moment that is easy to walk past if you always play solo or keep your wanted level low.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: Play with your partner alongside you.
Commit crimes until the wanted level reaches 4 stars.
Break line of sight and stay hidden until the heat dies down.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: This trophy is a chain: rob three shops in a row, with your partner, without ever losing your wanted level between them. The trick is speed and planning — pick three shops close together, plan the route in advance, and move fast so the police never catch up between robberies. Keep the wanted level alive the whole way: if it drops to zero before the third shop, the chain breaks and you start over.
trophies.missableNote: A three-shop chain that must be done in one run with your partner, keeping the wanted level alive throughout — miss the chain and the attempt resets.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Choose three shops close together and plan the route.
Rob the first shop with your partner present.
Move fast to the next two, keeping the wanted level active, and finish the third.

trophies.guide: Leonida is full of vehicles, and this trophy counts the distinct ones you discover — driving a new model, or even just getting close to one, adds it to the list. The counter climbs naturally as you play, but you can push it along by visiting car parks, dealerships, docks and airports, where rare models park. If a vehicle type is eluding you, try different districts and times of day, since traffic varies by area.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Drive and explore — new vehicle models count as you discover them.
Visit car parks, dealerships, docks and airports for rarer models.
Reach 100 discovered vehicles.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aiming mode, and this trophy needs 5 takedowns inside a single activation. The setup matters more than the shooting: find a group of enemies clustered together, activate Combat Focus when they are all in view, and work through them quickly before the meter runs out. A busy shootout or a room full of enemies is the right moment — do not waste the activation on one or two targets.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
steps: Find a fight with five or more enemies close together.
Activate Combat Focus with them all in view.
Down 5 enemies before the focus ends.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is the Vice City airport, and this trophy is about leaving it in a way the airport did not schedule — stealing a plane and taking off, or otherwise departing without a ticket. The simplest read is to get to the airfield, take an aircraft, and get airborne. Expect security and police attention the moment you do, so be ready to fly low and fast once you are up.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to a specific stunt at a specific place — the airport departure only counts if you leave VCIA by aircraft rather than through the front doors.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
steps: Get to VCIA airfield, on foot or by vehicle.
Take an aircraft on the runway.
Take off for an unscheduled departure.

trophies.guide: Rhinos are the game's tanks, and this trophy is about dealing with them — the description's joke is that it gets hot inside one. The practical route is to encounter a Rhino, which usually means a high wanted level or a military area, and either take it over or survive its attention. If you can commandeer one, driving it around counts toward the spirit of the trophy; if not, destroying or escaping one still moves you toward it.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
steps: Reach a high wanted level or a military area to draw out a Rhino.
Take it over if you can, or deal with it from cover.
Complete the encounter to earn the trophy.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: This is a stealth trophy: rob a jewelry store and get away without ever being detected. That means casing the store first, moving quietly, avoiding cameras and staff sightlines, and leaving before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — abort, lose the heat, and try again with a slower, quieter approach.
trophies.missableNote: One failed detection ends the attempt, so a loud first try wastes the run — plan the route and go in quiet.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
steps: Case the jewelry store: note cameras, staff and exits.
Enter quietly and take the goods without being seen.
Leave undetected to complete the robbery.

trophies.guide: Bank vaults are the high-stakes robberies of the game, and this silver trophy needs five of them robbed with a successful escape each time. Each vault is its own job — plan the approach, crack the vault, grab the take and get out clean. Five successful escapes is a grind, so treat each vault as a separate heist: prepare, execute, escape, and repeat until the fifth one pops the trophy.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Find bank vault robbery opportunities on the map.
Rob a vault and escape with the take.
Repeat until 5 vaults are robbed and escaped.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks roam Leonida's roads, and this trophy needs you to rob one and escape. The classic approach is to block or ram the truck to a stop, deal with its guards, take the cash and get away before the police lock on. Pick a quiet stretch of road away from police patrols, strike fast, and have a getaway vehicle ready — the escape is half the trophy.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Find an armored truck on the road.
Stop it, deal with the guards and take the cash.
Escape the police to complete the robbery.

trophies.guide: This trophy asks you to visit every area of Leonida, from Vice City's streets to the swamps and small towns of the wider state. The game's map tracks which areas you have visited, so the job is a systematic sweep: work through the map district by district, driving or flying into each named area until it registers. Pair it with the collectible hunts — cards, meditation spots and WAiNK locations all sit in the same far corners.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: Open the map and note which areas are still unvisited.
Sweep the state district by district, entering each named area.
Visit every area to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Leonida's gangs each run illegal operations — fronts and hideouts you can hit — and this trophy needs one robbery from each gang's operation. That means finding each gang's turf, identifying its operation, and robbing it. The gangs are spread across the state, so this trophy doubles as a tour of their territories; take them one gang at a time and tick each off as you go.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Learn which gangs hold territory and where their operations are.
Rob one illegal operation for a gang.
Repeat for every gang until all are hit.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach is Vice City's beachfront strip, and this trophy is a quiet one: find a bar with a view, order a cocktail, and enjoy it. There is no combat and no timer — just go to the right spot, sit down with a drink, and let the moment register. It is the kind of trophy best grabbed during an early Vice City visit, before the story pulls you elsewhere.
trophies.missableNote: A small moment tied to one beachfront spot — easy to walk past forever if you never stop for a drink on Ocean Beach.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
steps: Head to Ocean Beach in Vice City.
Find a bar or spot with a view of the beach.
Order and enjoy a cocktail there.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: This trophy is a throwback moment: get into a vehicle inside a showroom and smash your way out through the glass in classic GTA style. Find a vehicle showroom, get behind the wheel of a car inside it, and drive straight out through the front. It is a one-and-done stunt — loud, simple, and best attempted when you do not mind the wanted level that follows.
trophies.missableNote: A single scripted-style stunt in one place — once you have left the showroom normally, you have to set the moment up again deliberately.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
steps: Find a vehicle showroom with cars on display.
Get into a car inside the showroom.
Drive out through the front glass.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Kolt & Associates runs a bowling alley, and this trophy is about following through there — playing a game of bowling to its end. Head to the alley, start a game, and bowl through all the frames. You do not need a high score; finishing the game is what counts, and the trophy pops when the last frame is done.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Start a game of bowling.
Play through to the end of the game.

trophies.guide: This trophy is about a partnership moment that draws a crowd — a story beat where you and your partner do something the public notices. It unlocks through the story, so keep playing the main missions and it will arrive on its own. If you are chasing it deliberately, look for the mission where the partnership takes centre stage and play it through to its conclusion.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to a specific partnership story beat — it only fires during that moment, so it is worth knowing it exists before you play past it.
trophies.name: Personal Best
steps: Progress the story to the partnership set piece.
Play the mission through to its conclusion.
The trophy unlocks at the beat's end.

trophies.guide: This trophy tracks choices — decisions you make across the game, for better or worse. It pops once you have made enough of them, so the way to earn it is to keep engaging with the game's choice moments instead of skipping past them: dialogue options, moral calls in missions, and side decisions all feed it. If you tend to rush through conversations, slow down for the ones that offer a real choice.
trophies.missableNote: Choices are one-time by nature — a decision made cannot be unmade in that playthrough, so engage with choice moments as they appear.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
steps: Play the story and engage with dialogue and mission choices.
Make decisions at the choice moments instead of skipping them.
The trophy pops once enough choices are made.

trophies.guide: This trophy is about succeeding on a second try — failing something once, then coming back and nailing it. The natural way to earn it is to fail a mission or activity, retry it, and complete it on the next attempt. Do not be afraid of a failed attempt early on: in this game, the second try is its own trophy, so a retry after a stumble is progress, not a setback.
trophies.missableNote: It needs a failure followed by a success — if you never fail anything, you never trigger it, so a deliberate retry counts.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
steps: Attempt a mission or activity and fail it once.
Retry it immediately.
Complete it on the second attempt to unlock the trophy.

trophies.guide: This is the game's oddity trophy — it unlocks when you witness something strange in Leonida, the kind of event players talk about afterwards. Strange happenings hide in out-of-the-way places and at odd hours, so explore the map's quieter corners, visit unusual landmarks, and keep an eye out for anything that does not fit. It is a trophy that rewards curiosity more than skill.
trophies.missableNote: A one-off strange event in a specific place — you have to be there when it happens, so it is the easiest trophy to walk past without knowing.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
steps: Explore Leonida's unusual landmarks and quiet corners.
Visit them at different times, including at night.
Trigger the strange event to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by means striking someone from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon, and this trophy needs you to bowl someone over that way. The setup is simple: get a melee weapon, drive slowly past a target on foot, and swing as you pass. A quiet street with pedestrians is the place to try it — keep your speed low so the swing connects, and one clean hit is enough.
trophies.missableNote: A single specific stunt from a moving vehicle — it only counts if the hit lands as a melee drive-by, so a gun or a ram does not trigger it.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Equip a melee weapon and get into a vehicle.
Drive slowly past a pedestrian.
Strike them with the melee weapon as you pass.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are dirty money you earn from certain jobs, and laundering them through your contacts turns them clean — this trophy needs $250,000 laundered in total. The count is cumulative, so every laundering run adds up; keep feeding marked bills to your contacts whenever you have them rather than letting them pile up. It pairs well with the robbery trophies, since those jobs are a steady source of marked bills.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
steps: Earn Marked Bills from jobs and robberies.
Launder them through your contacts.
Reach $250,000 laundered in total.

trophies.guide: This trophy counts every dollar spent across all of Leonida's shops — clothes, weapons, food, vehicles and more — until the total hits $100,000. It builds up naturally across a playthrough, especially once you start buying weapons and vehicles, but you can finish it deliberately by spending big at the end: a car or a weapon purchase closes the gap fast. The tracker in this guide counts it as an economy trophy, so check it during cleanup.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Spend money at shops as you play — weapons, clothes, food and vehicles all count.
Track your total spending in the stats screen.
Make a big purchase at the end to close the gap to $100,000.

trophies.guide: Garage properties are buyable safehouses with storage for your vehicles, and this trophy needs all of them purchased. They are scattered across Leonida and each one costs money, so this is a late-game purchase — save up, then buy them one by one. Check the property map or in-game listings to find every garage, and the trophy pops when the last deed is yours.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Find the garage properties for sale across Leonida.
Save up the money to buy them.
Purchase the last garage to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app lets you register vehicles, and this trophy needs 10 of them registered. The flow is simple: find a vehicle, register it through the app, and repeat with nine more distinct vehicles. Any vehicles you already own or discover while exploring count, so this pairs well with the discover-100-vehicles trophy — register the interesting ones as you find them and the count climbs on its own.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app on the in-game phone.
Register a vehicle you have found or own.
Repeat with 9 more vehicles to reach 10.
